why: fix round on the flaky L17 long-line check: the cause is the test, not the product. Chromium scrolls the input to its caret in the key's own task, after the render that key caused, so the render's follow reads the old scroll; the scroll event moves the layer in the next frame, before that frame's animation callbacks. A probe of 40 keys per run, three runs, found the layer one scroll behind right after the key on 24 to 27 of 40 keys, and on 0 of about 514 drawn frames. The check now waits one drawn frame before it measures. Headless Chromium, browser half of next/apps/fabrika/e2e/fabsh.visual.test.ts: the old check failed 26 of 30 runs in a row, all on L17; the fixed check passed 50 of 50. No fast law can hold it: the rule needs a real layout and scroll. Also: the file's comments say it runs only on the 3-hour schedule or a visual run a pull request asks for (0536). The name_taken row keeps rule bug: no rule in 0035's closed list fits it, and the schema is not this round's to change.
